zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 開篇固定收益論點

核心通膨放緩，支出、投資與房市數據也轉弱，帶動美國公債在5月28日收高，中長天期漲勢較強。10年期殖利率下降3個基點至4.45%，2年期則僅下降1個基點；投資人仍認為，聯準會年底前升息的機率超過一半。

這波漲勢來自實質殖利率下降，10年期通膨補償並未改變。4月核心PCE月增率降至0.2%，但通膨年增率仍高，聯準會官員對現行政策究竟有多大抑制力，也有不同看法。John Williams主張等待更多證據；Alberto Musalem則警告，若未來一至兩季通膨未能恢復降溫，可能有必要升息。

7年期公債標售需求穩健，附買回市場現金充裕，協助市場消化供給，股票與信用債基金也同步上漲。不過，個別借款人的待遇差異明顯：槓桿收購前景使Caesars債務價格下跌，Sophos即使大幅提高再融資定價，仍被放款人要求更多保障。銀行資本債與結構化AI融資持續吸引資金，交易條款則決定了風險最終落在誰身上。

## 需求放緩，聯準會仍對通膨保持警戒

4月所得與支出報告顯示，通膨月增率降溫，家庭購買力卻也幾乎沒有增加。個人所得持平，低於市場預期的成長0.4%，前月增幅為0.5%；可支配所得下降0.1%。名目消費如預期增加0.5%，實質消費僅增0.1%，家庭儲蓄也下滑。

整體PCE物價月增0.4%，低於預期的0.5%，也較前值0.7%放緩；核心PCE月增0.2%，同樣比預期低0.1個百分點。但拉長比較期間，整體與核心PCE年增率仍分別為3.8%與3.3%，通膨壓力尚未明顯解除。

經濟成長也比初估疲弱。第一季GDP年化季增率由2.0%下修至1.6%，主要反映投資與消費支出下調。實質國內所得總額（GDI）成長0.9%，GDP與GDI的平均增幅為1.2%。初領失業救濟金人數由修正後的21萬人增至21.5萬人，高於市場預期的21.1萬人，四週平均升至20.9萬人。經濟仍在擴張，但需求壓力減輕，使進一步提高實質利率的理由減弱。

耐久財訂單的強勁表現，則主要由飛機帶動。總訂單大增7.9%，高於預期的3.9%，其中運輸設備增加21.5%。扣除運輸設備後，訂單仍增1.1%，但更貼近企業設備投資的扣除飛機非國防資本財訂單反而下降1.1%。企業投資意願因此不像整體數字所呈現的那麼強。

房市更直接反映高融資成本的壓力。新建單戶住宅銷售年化戶數由修正後的66.3萬戶降至62.2萬戶，不及預期的66萬戶，也較一年前減少11.3%。庫存升至48.9萬戶，供應月數由8.7個月增加至9.4個月，房價中位數為$42萬2,500。交易速度放慢，讓建商面臨更多待售房屋。

這些數據帶動10年期抗通膨公債實質殖利率下降3個基點至2.06%，跌幅與名目10年期殖利率相同；對應的損益兩平通膨率維持2.39%。其他天期實質殖利率也下降，5年期與7年期各跌3個基點至1.61%與1.83%，20年期與30年期則各跌2個基點。經濟活動轉弱，降低投資人要求的實質報酬，但能源成本與通膨預期上升的風險，仍支撐通膨補償。

附息公債漲勢以較長天期為主。2年期殖利率下降1個基點至3.99%，5年期下降2個基點至4.15%，30年期下降3個基點至4.98%。2s10s利差收窄2個基點至46個基點，2s30s也收窄2個基點至99個基點。2s5s10s蝶式利差維持負14個基點，5年期附近並未出現獨立的價格失衡。

Musalem的談話說明了短端漲勢受限的原因。他認為通膨風險已高於就業風險，實質政策利率也低於他估計的中性水準；若未來一至兩季通膨未能恢復下降，便可能需要升息。他並提醒，不能因期待生產力提高，就忽略當前通膨、逐漸上移的通膨預期，以及仍然穩定的勞動市場。截至週四，期貨定價顯示年底前升息的機率超過50%。

Williams的立場較有耐心。他表示，目前3.5%至3.75%的目標區間已對經濟產生一定抑制，聯準會可以先觀察戰爭、關稅與後續數據，並預期相關價格漲幅將在未來數月達到高峰。對於生產力，他強調真正的轉變難以即時辨識，長期而言也可能推高均衡實質利率。這種立場容許央行等待通膨衝擊的後續發展，卻不意味著預期中的AI生產力成長已足以支持立即寬鬆。

美國財政部$440億的7年期公債標售獲得廣泛的非交易商需求，得標利率為4.290%，投標倍數2.52倍。間接投標者取得獲接受競爭性投標的78.39%，直接投標者占11.19%，交易商占10.42%。交易商承接比例偏低，有助市場消化這批中期公債；新券將於6月1日發行及交割。

最短天期國庫券的殖利率並未跟著下降，即使擔保融資市場現金充裕。4、6、8與13週券的附息等值殖利率各上升1個基點，落在3.68%至3.70%；17至52週券則持平。相較於附息公債的漲勢，國庫券仍反映市場對政策轉鬆缺乏把握。

股市與債市同步收高。S&P 500上漲0.58%，Nasdaq 100上漲0.84%，半導體指數上漲1.00%，VIX下降3.38%至15.74。折現率降低有利成長股，市場尚未把較弱的經濟數據解讀為企業獲利將陷入衰退。美元指數下跌0.19%至99.02，也減輕了依賴美元融資者的短期壓力。

能源仍是通膨展望中較難安心的一環。WTI上漲0.25%至$88.90，Brent下跌0.62%至$93.71；儘管兩者單週跌幅均超過7%，油價仍高，成本繼續轉嫁至其他價格的風險未退。黃金上漲1.16%至$4,499.30，即使股市走強、波動率下降，通膨、地緣政治與政策避險需求仍在。

## 融資便宜，信用市場待遇卻大不相同

信用債基金隨美國公債上漲，LQD升0.30%、HYG升0.12%、JNK升0.10%，EMB升0.26%。股市走強、融資條件寬鬆之際，高收益債基金漲幅仍溫和，幾筆大型交易更顯示放款人對個別借款人的判斷差距。

Caesars同意由Fertitta Entertainment收購後，其2032年到期、票息6%的無擔保債券下跌逾1美分，至每$1面額報價89美分；$28億的定期貸款也下跌約0.5美分，成交價介於96至97美分。交易對Caesars股權的估值為$57億，並將承接約$119億債務。市場分析估計，可能增加約$60億淨負債，融資由10家銀行承諾提供。

自2月傳出收購消息以來，Caesars無擔保債券已下跌逾8美分。合併後的公司雖能擴大規模，債權人卻面臨槓桿提高、融資條款未定，以及受償順位可能落後新債的風險。買方支付的股權溢價，對債權人的處境幫助有限。

附買回市場則有大量現金。5月約$1,200億流入貨幣市場基金，美國財政部在稅期後削減逾$2,700億國庫券供給，現金管理買回也進一步減少擔保品。附買回利率低於聯準會目標區間下限，SOFR僅略高於3.50%，低於4月約3.65%的平均值。融資成本降低，有利交易商持有美國公債與信用債庫存。

銀行承作這些部位的空間也變大。強化補充槓桿比率的規則調整，擴大大型銀行中介美國公債交易的能力；Wells Fargo解除資產上限後持續擴張，也增加附買回融資供給。美國八家全球系統重要性銀行第一季資產合計增加$1.3兆，其中包括$3,000億附賣回交易，以及約$1,000億美國公債交易部位。這項結構性擴張協助市場承接龐大庫存與新券，未出現明顯融資壓力。

歐洲銀行利用投資人對次順位債收益的需求，延長資本融資期限。Santander發行$15億AT1債券，10年內不得贖回；NatWest發行£5億債券，票息7.5%，可於2036年贖回。這類較長不可贖回期的結構，占今年主要貨幣AT1發行量的25%，創歷來新高，相較慣常的五年贖回期，額外利差卻不大。

發行人付出約300個基點的利差，即可取得長達10年的第一類資本融資。投資人沿五至10年期的平坦利差曲線，只取得有限的額外補償，卻要更長時間承受利率波動、展期與次級市場流動性不足的風險。銀行鎖定再融資條件之際，債券對這些風險重新定價的緩衝相對有限。

AI基礎設施融資採用另一套保障安排。Apollo與Blackstone正為約$360億的延遲動用債務尋找投資人，資金與Anthropic購買Google TPU晶片有關。擬議架構包括約$60億A1票據、$250億A2票據，以及$45億次順位B票據，於本週徵集認購，預計下週完成。

若租賃違約後出售晶片的收入不足以償還投資人，Broadcom提供的殘值保障將彌補優先A級分券的缺口。因此，優先票據的信用風險更貼近Broadcom的投資等級信用，而不是Anthropic本身的獲利。優先順位、延遲動用與可供租賃的實體資產，使新創公司的融資需求得以拆成風險不同的債權。

Pimco的觀察顯示，整個市場的差距已相當大。資料中心高收益債約有$400億，占美國高收益債市場2.7%，並屬於全球超大規模雲端業者逾$2,500億借款的一部分。其中約75%的利差接近6%，其餘則達10%以上。Pimco偏好投資等級承購方、不可取消的合約、能在合約到期前完成還款，以及期末仍有資產殘值的安排，以區分有合約現金流支撐的交易與投機性擴產。

軟體業借款人的談判較為艱難。Thoma Bravo提出$25億Sophos再融資案，初步條件接近基準利率加600個基點，遠高於既有債務約加350個基點，多家放款機構仍拒絕參與。Sophos有一筆$21億貸款將於2027年3月到期，標普已將相關實體的展望調降為負向。面對AI衝擊與高槓桿，考慮同意展期約2.5年的既有放款人要求股東投入更多資本、先償還部分本金，並提高定價。

另一宗爭議涉及Water Station Management債券的擔保資產。352 Capital的基金投資人指控，飲水機擔保品缺失或根本不存在，經理人也涉及個人利益衝突，基金仍投入數百萬美元購債。相關訴訟與刑事指控稱，宣稱用於購置販賣機的資金，主要被拿來支付或買斷加盟商。爭議集中在擔保品、利益衝突與資金用途，與整體信用市場是否有資金供給是不同問題。

## 通膨壓力使各國央行維持戒心

歐洲央行4月29日至30日會議紀要顯示，當時距離升息已相當接近，多位官員表示即使升息也不會反對。歐元區通膨率為3%，決策官員擔心能源成本進一步傳導至薪資與通膨預期。首席經濟學家Philip Lane警告，即使伊朗戰爭最初造成的衝擊消退，第二輪效應仍可能持續。海外緊縮預期也讓美國殖利率更難持續大幅下降。

日本殖利率上升，愈來愈多反映通膨波動、財政疑慮、政府供給增加與央行支持減少。伊朗戰爭爆發以來，10年期日本公債期限溢價已上升近70個基點，市場通膨預期升至至少2004年以來最高。殖利率提高之際，日圓仍然走弱，較像是投資人要求補償通膨與財政風險，而不是日圓資產的收益吸引力改善。

更高的殖利率也改變日本儲蓄者的選擇。10年期日本公債殖利率自2008年以來首次高於東證股價指數股息殖利率，公司債殖利率則升至指數2000年編製以來最高。國內債券成為股票及匯率避險後外國債券更具競爭力的替代選項，企業再融資成本卻也隨之增加。若資金轉向日本，其他主權債市場可能需要提供更高期限溢價才能留住需求。

美國收盤後、週五公布的東京5月通膨報告顯示，不含生鮮食品的核心CPI年增率降至1.3%，連續第六個月放緩，增幅為四年來最低。不含生鮮食品與能源的指標上升1.6%。水費、汽油與育兒補貼壓低通膨，但食品價格轉嫁與弱勢日圓仍帶來上行風險。隔夜指數交換定價顯示，日本央行6月15日至16日升息的機率仍約為77%。

南非已先行緊縮。南非央行將基準利率提高25個基點至7%，為2023年以來首次升息，理由是重疊的通膨衝擊可能引發第二輪效應。南非幣兌美元維持0.2%漲幅，10年期政府公債殖利率扭轉盤中升勢，收於8.62%，比當日高點低9個基點，股市則下跌。債市反應顯示通膨風險溢價有所緩解，但央行警告可能進一步緊縮，也意味經濟成長仍須承受代價。

巴西考慮的則是暫停降息。央行貨幣政策主管Nilton David指出，2028年通膨預期惡化，央行不會容許外部價格衝擊使通膨在政策評估期間內偏離目標。5月上旬通膨年增率加速至4.64%，高於3%目標；Selic利率在4月由先前維持的15%高點調降後，目前為14.5%。

4月新增就業低於所有分析師預測，削弱了官員先前視為通膨降溫阻力的勞動市場韌性。不過，能源成本上升與財政不確定性，仍壓縮繼續寬鬆的空間。若6月暫停降息，國內利率將維持限制性，讓央行有時間評估這些壓力。

## 主權借款人的籌資考驗各不相同

人口老化、退休金與醫療支出、戰略投資，以及各國融資成本上升，持續壓迫歐盟成員國預算，法國因此主張擴大聯合舉債。共同債務可利用歐盟較強的整體信用籌資，也有助銀行分散過度集中的本國主權債部位。同時，超國家債券供給增加，將在各國發債之外形成更大的基準債市場，與其他債券競逐全球儲蓄資金。

阿根廷各省與布宜諾斯艾利斯市已在海外找到買家。2026年前五個月合計籌資$23億，速度為2017年以來同期最快，資金主要用於再融資與延長到期期限。布宜諾斯艾利斯市發行$5億10年期債券，殖利率7.4%，獲約$30億認購；科爾多瓦省發行$8億，殖利率8.95%，丘布特省發行$6.5億、殖利率9.45%，恩特雷里奧斯省發行$3億、殖利率9.6%。

相較之下，聯邦政府仍仰賴短天期本地融資，未選擇以接近9%的殖利率到海外發債。在本地交易的主權美元債，2027年選舉前到期券殖利率約5.1%，選舉後到期券則約8.6%。丘布特省以石油權利金提供額外擔保，但各省仍需依賴央行的美元償付外幣債務，過去也曾在主權危機期間重整債務。部分省債認購強勁，與外匯存底及選舉風險仍然並存。

塞內加爾近期的重點是履行債務與國際貨幣基金（IMF）談判。2037年到期歐元債券的€5,375萬利息將於6月8日支付，IMF同日將展開訪問；2031年到期美元債券另有$3,875萬款項，須於6月10日支付。投資人預期付款會如期進行，但政府與IMF仍在討論新方案是否必須以債務重整為前提，因此態度謹慎。

隱藏公共債務曝光後，IMF已於2024年暫停一項$18億計畫，塞內加爾政治領導層則以威脅主權為由反對重整。債券價格偏低之際，投資人關注的不只是即將到期的利息，還包括恢復IMF融資的條件能否明朗。

## 前瞻市場意涵

接下來的經濟數據，將顯示支出、設備需求與房市的疲弱是否延續至第二季。貿易與庫存初值將於5月29日08:30美東時間公布，製造業ISM與服務業ISM則分別於6月1日、6月3日10:00公布。除了商品貿易逆差與庫存累積，新訂單、就業及支付價格分項尤其值得注意。若需求與投入價格同步降溫，將支持實質殖利率續降，五至10年期可能最為敏感；若經濟保持韌性、成本壓力再起，實質殖利率與通膨補償都可能上升。

勞動數據有助釐清Williams主張等待與Musalem擔心通膨持續的差異。JOLTS將於6月2日10:00美東時間公布，ADP為6月3日08:15，初領失業救濟金則為6月4日08:30，均在6月17日至18日聯準會會議之前。職缺減少、聘僱轉弱且初領人數再次增加，將削弱年底前升息的理由；若職缺穩定、聘僱改善、初領人數回落，通膨支持緊縮的論點就更強，2年期公債最直接受到影響。

美國財政部另有兩項買回操作。6月3日的流動性支持買回涵蓋20至30年期名目附息公債，上限$20億，6月4日交割；6月4日的現金管理買回涵蓋一個月至兩年期附息公債，上限$125億，6月5日交割。隨國庫券供給與附息債交割補充市場擔保品，報價品質、交割及附買回利率將反映交易商融通庫存的餘裕。若融資有序、附買回利率維持低於第一季常態，將有利長債與待發行信用債；若利率明顯回升至正常水準或出現交割壓力，近期現金充裕帶來的好處便會受到考驗。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rose on May 28 as slower core inflation and weaker spending, investment and housing data brought some relief to the longer end of the market. The 10-year yield fell 3 basis points to 4.45%, while the 2-year declined just 1 basis point as investors continued to price a greater-than-even chance of a Federal Reserve increase by year-end.

The gains came through lower real yields, with 10-year inflation compensation unchanged. April's core PCE increase slowed to 0.2%, but annual inflation remained elevated and Fed officials differed over how much restraint current policy was providing. John Williams favored waiting for more evidence; Alberto Musalem warned that a failure to resume disinflation over the next quarter or two could warrant a hike.

A well-supported 7-year Treasury auction and plentiful repo cash helped the market absorb supply. Stocks and credit funds also advanced. Behind those aggregate gains, creditors were drawing sharper distinctions: Caesars debt fell on the prospect of a leveraged takeover, and lenders sought more protection in a Sophos refinancing even at substantially higher pricing. Banks and structured AI financings continued to attract capital, with the terms determining who ultimately bore the risk.

## Softer Demand Meets a Wary Fed

April's income and spending figures combined a softer monthly inflation reading with little growth in purchasing power. Personal income was unchanged, against expectations for a 0.4% increase and a 0.5% gain the previous month. Disposable income slipped 0.1%. Nominal consumption rose 0.5%, as forecast, but real consumption increased only 0.1%, while household saving fell.

Headline PCE prices rose 0.4% on the month, below the 0.5% consensus and down from 0.7%. Core prices increased 0.2%, also 0.1 percentage point less than expected. Annual headline and core inflation remained at 3.8% and 3.3%, respectively, leaving a much less reassuring picture over the longer comparison period.

Growth was also weaker than first estimated. Q1 GDP was revised to a 1.6% annualized pace from 2.0%, largely because of lower investment and consumer spending. Real gross domestic income grew 0.9%; the average of GDP and GDI increased 1.2%. Initial jobless claims rose to 215,000 from a revised 210,000, exceeding the 211,000 consensus, and the four-week average reached 209,000. The figures still showed expansion, but with less demand pressure to justify higher real rates.

An aircraft-driven surge in durable-goods orders masked a decline in underlying equipment demand. Total orders jumped 7.9%, against a 3.9% forecast, as transportation equipment increased 21.5%. Orders excluding transportation rose 1.1%, yet nondefense capital-goods orders excluding aircraft fell 1.1%. That last measure gave businesses' investment plans a weaker cast than the headline suggested.

Housing showed the strain from high financing costs more directly. New single-family home sales fell to an annualized 622,000 from a revised 663,000, below the 660,000 consensus and 11.3% lower than a year earlier. Inventory rose to 489,000 homes, taking supply to 9.4 months from 8.7, with a median price of $422,500. Slower turnover left builders with more homes to clear.

The data helped pull the 10-year TIPS yield down 3 basis points to 2.06%, matching the decline in the nominal 10-year yield. The corresponding breakeven stayed at 2.39%. The real-yield decline extended across maturities: 5- and 7-year TIPS yields each fell 3 basis points to 1.61% and 1.83%, while 20- and 30-year yields fell 2. Investors required a lower real return as activity softened, while energy costs and the risk of higher inflation expectations continued to support inflation compensation.

The rally was stronger farther along the coupon curve. The 2-year yield closed at 3.99%, down 1 basis point; the 5-year fell 2 basis points to 4.15%; and the 30-year declined 3 basis points to 4.98%. The 2s10s curve flattened 2 basis points to 46, with 2s30s narrowing by the same amount to 99. An unchanged 2s5s10s butterfly at -14 basis points showed no separate dislocation around the 5-year sector.

Musalem's comments underscored the obstacle to a larger front-end rally. He judged inflation risks to be greater than employment risks and put the real policy rate below his estimate of neutral. If disinflation failed to resume over the next one or two quarters, he said, an increase could be justified. He also cautioned against using prospective productivity gains to discount current inflation, drifting expectations or a stable labor market. As of Thursday, futures assigned more than a 50% chance to a hike by year-end.

Williams saw the current 3.5%-3.75% target range as exerting some restraint and said the Fed could wait to assess the war, tariffs and incoming data. He expected the associated pace of price increases to peak in coming months. On productivity, he stressed both the difficulty of identifying genuine shifts in real time and the possibility that they eventually raise equilibrium real rates. His more patient stance left room to observe the inflation shock, without treating a hoped-for AI productivity boom as a reason to ease immediately.

Treasury's $44 billion 7-year auction drew broad nondealer demand. The sale stopped at 4.290%, with a 2.52 bid-to-cover ratio. Indirect bidders received 78.39% of accepted competitive bids, direct bidders 11.19%, and dealers 10.42%. The low dealer allocation helped the market take down the intermediate-maturity supply; issuance and settlement are scheduled for June 1.

At the shortest maturities, bills remained firmer in yield despite abundant secured-funding cash. Coupon-equivalent yields on 4-, 6-, 8- and 13-week bills rose 1 basis point to between 3.68% and 3.70%, while 17- through 52-week yields were unchanged. That contrast with coupons was consistent with a policy outlook still resistant to easing.

Stocks rose alongside bonds. The S&P 500 gained 0.58%, the Nasdaq 100 advanced 0.84%, and the semiconductor index added 1.00%; the VIX fell 3.38% to 15.74. Lower discount rates were helping growth stocks without softer activity being priced as an earnings recession. The dollar index slipped 0.19% to 99.02, easing the immediate pressure on dollar-funded borrowers.

Energy remained a less comfortable part of the inflation outlook. WTI rose 0.25% to $88.90, while Brent fell 0.62% to $93.71. Both were down more than 7% for the week, but their still-elevated levels left scope for costs to pass through to other prices. Gold gained 1.16% to $4,499.30, retaining inflation, geopolitical and policy-hedging demand even as equities strengthened and volatility receded.

## Cheap Funding, Uneven Credit Demand

Credit funds gained with Treasuries: LQD rose 0.30%, HYG 0.12%, JNK 0.10%, and EMB 0.26%. The modest high-yield gains accompanied better equities and easier funding, while several large transactions showed how differently lenders were assessing individual borrowers.

Caesars' 6% unsecured bond due in 2032 fell more than 1 cent to 89 cents on the dollar after the company agreed to be bought by Fertitta Entertainment. Its $2.8 billion term loan lost about half a cent, trading between 96 and 97. The deal valued Caesars' equity at $5.7 billion and included the assumption of about $11.9 billion of debt. Market analysis pointed to roughly $6 billion of potential net new debt, with financing committed by 10 banks.

Caesars' unsecured bonds had already fallen more than 8 cents since takeover reports emerged in February. The enlarged company would gain scale, but creditors faced higher leverage, uncertain financing terms and the possibility of a weaker position beneath newly raised debt. The premium paid for the equity offered them little immediate comfort.

Elsewhere, repo markets were awash with cash. About $120 billion had entered money-market funds during May, while Treasury's post-tax reduction in bill supply exceeded $270 billion. Cash-management buybacks further reduced collateral relative to available cash. Repo rates traded below the lower bound of the Fed's target range, and SOFR was just above 3.50%, compared with an April average of about 3.65%. The cheaper financing supported dealers carrying Treasury and credit inventories.

Banks had more capacity to intermediate those positions as well. Changes to the enhanced supplementary leverage ratio expanded the room for large-bank Treasury intermediation, and Wells Fargo's growth after removal of its asset cap added repo financing. The eight U.S. global systemically important banks increased assets by a combined $1.3 trillion in Q1, including $300 billion of reverse repos and about $100 billion in Treasury trading books. That structural expansion helped accommodate large inventories and new issuance without visible funding stress.

European banks used strong demand for subordinated income to extend the life of their capital funding. Santander sold a $1.5 billion Additional Tier 1 bond with a 10-year non-call period. NatWest issued £500 million callable in 2036 with a 7.5% coupon. Long-call structures accounted for an unprecedented 25% of major-currency AT1 issuance this year, as the extra spread over the customary five-year call was relatively small.

For issuers, about 300 basis points of spread could secure a decade of Tier 1 financing. Investors received limited additional compensation along a flat five- to 10-year spread curve while taking longer exposure to rate volatility, extension risk and a less liquid secondary market. Banks were locking in refinancing certainty on terms that left less room for a repricing of those risks.

AI infrastructure offered a different set of protections. Apollo and Blackstone were seeking investors for roughly $36 billion of delayed-draw debt tied to Anthropic's purchases of Google's TPU chips. The proposed financing included about $6 billion of A1 notes, $25 billion of A2 notes and $4.5 billion of junior B notes. Orders were requested during the week, with completion expected the following week.

Broadcom's residual-value support would cover senior A-tranche shortfalls if, after a lease default, sales of the chips failed to repay investors. That backstop linked the senior notes more closely to Broadcom's investment-grade credit than to Anthropic's standalone earnings. Seniority, delayed draws and leased hard assets allowed the startup's financing needs to be divided into claims with different risk profiles.

Pimco's assessment of the wider market showed how large that dispersion had become. Data-center junk debt totaled roughly $40 billion, or 2.7% of U.S. high yield, within more than $250 billion of global hyperscaler borrowing. About 75% traded at spreads near 6%, with the remainder at 10% or wider. Pimco favored investment-grade offtakers, non-cancellable contracts, repayment before contract expiry and residual asset value—protections that distinguish contracted cash flow from speculative capacity.

Software borrowers faced tougher negotiations. Several lenders passed on Thoma Bravo's proposed $2.5 billion Sophos refinancing even with early terms approaching 600 basis points over the benchmark, versus about 350 basis points on existing debt. Sophos has a $2.1 billion loan maturing in March 2027, and S&P had changed the relevant entity's outlook to negative. Existing lenders considering an extension of roughly 2.5 years sought more sponsor equity, partial repayment and higher pricing as AI disruption and leverage weighed on the refinancing case.

A separate dispute concerned the assets backing Water Station Management bonds. Investors in 352 Capital alleged that the fund put millions of dollars into the bonds despite missing or nonexistent water-machine collateral and a personal conflict involving the manager. Lawsuits and criminal charges alleged that proceeds described as financing vending machines went mainly toward paying or buying out franchisees. The allegations centered on collateral, conflicts and use of proceeds, rather than the broader availability of credit.

## Inflation Keeps Central Banks on Guard

The ECB's account of its April 29-30 meeting revealed how close officials had come to raising rates. A number would not have opposed an increase. With euro-area inflation at 3%, their concern was that energy costs would feed into wages and expectations. Chief Economist Philip Lane warned that second-round effects could persist after the initial Iran-war shock faded. Overseas tightening expectations remained an obstacle to a more sustained decline in U.S. yields.

In Japan, rising yields increasingly reflected inflation volatility, fiscal concerns, greater government supply and reduced central-bank support. The 10-year JGB term premium had climbed almost 70 basis points since the Iran war began, and market inflation expectations were at their highest since at least 2004. The yen weakened even as yields rose, pointing to compensation for inflation and fiscal uncertainty rather than an improvement in the currency's income appeal.

Higher yields were changing the choices available to Japanese savers. The 10-year JGB yield exceeded the Topix dividend yield for the first time since 2008, while corporate bond yields reached their highest since the index began in 2000. Domestic bonds offered a more credible alternative to stocks and currency-hedged foreign bonds, even as refinancing became more expensive for companies. A shift in demand toward Japan could require other sovereign markets to offer a higher term premium.

Tokyo's May inflation report, released Friday after the U.S. close, showed the core measure excluding fresh food slowing to 1.3% year on year. It was the sixth consecutive deceleration and the weakest pace in four years. The measure excluding fresh food and energy rose 1.6%. Water, gasoline and childcare subsidies depressed inflation, while food-price pass-through and the weak yen sustained upside risk. Overnight-index swaps still put the probability of a June 15-16 BOJ hike at roughly 77%.

South Africa had already tightened. Its Reserve Bank raised the benchmark 25 basis points to 7%, the first increase since 2023, citing the danger that overlapping inflation shocks would generate second-round effects. The rand retained a 0.2% gain against the dollar. The 10-year government yield reversed an intraday increase to finish at 8.62%, 9 basis points below its session high, although equities fell. The bond response suggested some relief in the inflation-risk premium; the bank's warning of further tightening also left a cost to growth.

Brazil was weighing a pause in easing. Monetary Policy Director Nilton David highlighted worsening 2028 inflation expectations and said external price shocks would not be allowed to push inflation beyond the policy horizon. Annual inflation accelerated to 4.64% in early May, against a 3% target. The Selic stood at 14.5% following an April cut from the previously maintained 15% peak.

April job creation undershot every analyst forecast, softening the picture of labor resilience that policymakers had cited as an obstacle to disinflation. Even so, higher energy costs and fiscal uncertainty left less room for continued easing. A June pause would keep domestic interest rates restrictive while the bank assessed those pressures.

## Sovereign Borrowers Face Different Funding Tests

France was advocating more joint EU borrowing as aging populations, pension and health spending, strategic investment and higher national funding costs strained member budgets. Common debt would allow borrowing against the bloc's stronger collective credit and help banks diversify away from concentrated holdings of their home sovereigns. It would also add supranational bonds competing for global savings, broadening benchmark supply alongside national issuance.

Argentina's provinces and Buenos Aires City were already finding buyers abroad. They raised a combined $2.3 billion in the first five months of 2026, the fastest pace for that period since 2017, largely to refinance debt and extend maturities. Buenos Aires City drew about $3 billion in orders for a $500 million 10-year issue yielding 7.4%. Cordoba sold $800 million at 8.95%, Chubut $650 million at 9.45%, and Entre Rios $300 million at 9.6%.

The federal government, by contrast, continued to rely on short-dated local financing rather than borrow externally near a 9% yield. Locally traded sovereign dollar bonds yielded about 5.1% when maturing before the 2027 election and 8.6% afterward. Chubut's oil-royalty collateral offered additional security, but provinces still depended on central-bank dollars to service foreign-currency debt and had restructured during previous sovereign crises. Strong demand for selected provincial issues coexisted with reserve and election risks.

Senegal's immediate concern was debt service and negotiations with the IMF. A €53.75 million coupon on its 2037 euro bond falls due June 8, the day an IMF visit is scheduled to begin. Another $38.75 million payment, on its 2031 dollar bond, is due June 10. Investors expected the payments to be made but remained cautious while the government and Fund debated whether a new program would require restructuring.

The IMF suspended a $1.8 billion program in 2024 after hidden public debt came to light. Senegal's political leadership rejected restructuring as a threat to sovereignty. Low bond valuations therefore depended on more than the upcoming coupons: investors also needed clarity on the terms of renewed IMF financing.

## Forward Market Significance

The next activity releases will show whether weakness in spending, equipment demand and housing is carrying into Q2. Advance trade and inventory figures are due May 29 at 08:30 ET, followed by manufacturing ISM on June 1 and services ISM on June 3, both at 10:00 ET. New orders, employment and prices paid will be particularly useful alongside the goods deficit and inventory accumulation. Softer demand coupled with cooling input prices would support further real-yield relief, especially in the five- to 10-year sector; resilient activity and renewed cost pressure could lift both real yields and inflation compensation.

Labor reports will help resolve the difference between Williams's patient stance and Musalem's concern about persistent inflation. JOLTS is due June 2 at 10:00 ET, ADP June 3 at 08:15 ET, and jobless claims June 4 at 08:30 ET, ahead of the June 17-18 Fed meeting. Fewer openings, weaker hiring and another rise in claims would reduce the case for a year-end hike. Stable openings, better hiring and a reversal in claims would leave the inflation argument for tighter policy stronger, with the 2-year sector most directly exposed.

Treasury also has two buybacks scheduled. The June 3 liquidity-support operation covers 20- to 30-year nominal coupons, with a $2 billion cap and June 4 settlement. The June 4 cash-management operation covers one-month to two-year coupons, capped at $12.5 billion and settling June 5. Offer quality, settlement and repo rates will show how comfortably dealers can finance inventories as bill supply and coupon settlements replenish collateral. Orderly funding below Q1 repo norms would support the long end and the credit pipeline; a marked normalization in repo or settlement strain would put the recent benefit from abundant cash under pressure.

section_summaries.summary: Lower real yields drove a modest Treasury rally, but persistent inflation and the possibility of a Fed hike limited front-end gains. Credit funds advanced alongside equities, while leveraged borrowers faced more demanding lenders.

section_summaries.section_title: Softer Demand Meets a Wary Fed
section_summaries.summary: Income, investment and housing data weakened as monthly core inflation slowed. Williams favored waiting, while Musalem warned that stalled disinflation could justify a hike; the divergence helped keep the 2-year rally smaller than the long end's.
section_summaries.market_read: The 7-year auction drew broad nondealer demand, and stocks rose with bonds as real yields declined.

section_summaries.summary: Money-market inflows and greater bank intermediation kept repo financing cheap. Caesars and Sophos nevertheless faced tougher creditor scrutiny, while AT1 and AI infrastructure financings attracted demand on very different protections and terms.

section_summaries.section_title: Inflation Keeps Central Banks on Guard
section_summaries.summary: ECB officials had seriously considered a hike, Japan's higher yields were reshaping domestic investment choices, and South Africa tightened. Softer Japanese and Brazilian data complicated the outlook without removing inflation concerns.

section_summaries.section_title: Sovereign Borrowers Face Different Funding Tests
section_summaries.summary: France pressed for joint EU borrowing, Argentine provinces refinanced abroad despite federal funding constraints, and Senegal approached coupon payments and IMF talks. Access depended on each borrower's credit, collateral and policy position.

US trade, ISM and labor releases will clarify whether weaker demand can ease the Fed's inflation concerns. Treasury buybacks and settlement conditions will show whether plentiful repo cash continues to support bond inventories.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries gain as demand softens; creditors become more selective
overall_summary.session_narrative:
The 10-year Treasury yield fell 3 basis points to 4.45%, with the decline coming through real yields rather than inflation compensation. April income stalled, real spending barely increased and investment and housing figures weakened. Core PCE rose 0.2% on the month, below expectations, but elevated annual inflation left Fed officials divided over how much restraint policy was providing. Futures still put the chance of a year-end hike above 50%.

A well-supported 7-year auction and abundant repo cash helped absorb supply. Stocks and credit funds rose too, although individual borrowers faced sharply different terms. Caesars bonds fell after its proposed takeover raised leverage concerns; Sophos lenders sought more protection despite substantially higher refinancing pricing. European banks extended their capital funding, while a proposed Anthropic financing relied on Broadcom's residual-value support to protect senior investors.

Overseas, the ECB's debate over a hike and rising Japanese term premiums kept pressure on global borrowing costs. South Africa raised rates, while Brazil weighed weaker employment against persistent inflation. Upcoming US activity and labor releases will help determine whether lower real yields can spread to the policy-sensitive front end; Treasury buybacks will test whether funding remains easy as collateral supply rebuilds.
overall_summary.summary: Longer-dated Treasuries outperformed as slower core inflation and weaker demand lowered real yields. A possible Fed hike still weighed on the front end, while cheap funding did little to resolve the risks in leveraged takeovers and software refinancing.
